'Begs the question.'

Begging the question is often used to mean that something raises a question, but that's not what it actually means. What 'it begs the question' actually means is that your conclusion is based upon an unsupported premise.

Begging the question as a logical fallacy is this:

Ghosts are real because I have experienced something that can only be described as having seen a ghost.

Well of course everyone wants the new Glock 43, it's the hottest new model on the pistol market!

What it is not is:

Many people report things that they describe as having seen ghosts, which leads us to wonder whether ghosts are real.

The new Glock 43 is flying off the shelves, which makes us wonder what has caused this new model to be so wildly popular so soon after release.
